### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `18322b3cc70b9f7930232aad45a4053406d4ddf4` — the merge of head `74bc77a67ff1dc41b50928298f79a8b4cd1fad17` into base `d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 18322b3cc70b9f7930232aad45a4053406d4ddf4 && git checkout 18322b3cc70b9f7930232aad45a4053406d4ddf4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663 74bc77a67ff1dc41b50928298f79a8b4cd1fad17 && git checkout -B drift-repro d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663 && git merge --no-ff 74bc77a67ff1dc41b50928298f79a8b4cd1fad17

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4fbb4dbb655f1d1527eabeea0ef3af64f152663
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `3e77d606f8493901304c85a90be3b8a6763b6370`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- The fix is confined to `createSecurityCatalogReader(...).list('permission')` on the scoped, metadata-only branch (`type === 'permission' && scoped`, registry holds no holder of the name). Positions, capabilities, the unscoped by-name path and every registry-held name take the unchanged code; the `[#32867] CONTROL a name the registry holds` pin covers the last one. Red line "resolution is never loosened" holds: `resolveReference` / bare-name reads are untouched, and the D3 `ambiguous-in-environment` refusal is pinned in all four row orders.
- Holder address: package id, or `''` for a package-less row and the `sys_metadata` provenance sentinel; packages sort by id, `''` last; first row per `(package, name)` kept. Matches the registry path's shape (`permissionHolderEntries`).
- Every in-tree consumer of `catalog.list('permission')` already treats the list as one entry per holder (checked: `resolve-authz-context.ts` ledger holders + `platformPermissionSet`, `last-admin-guard.ts`, `agent-account-grant-refusal.ts`, `cleanup-package-permissions.ts`, `explain-engine.ts`, `suggested-audience-bindings.ts`, `runtime/.../catalog-activation.ts`). No consumer keys by bare name in a way that now double-counts.
- **should-fix S1 — an undeclared consumer move (new refusal).** `agent-account-grant-refusal.ts` `setBreaches`, on a refused (two-holder) read, judges "every holder of the name the catalog serves" (#32164 fail-closed). On the metadata-only path it saw only the first-listed row, so an agent-account grant (or a position binding the name) where only the *second-listed* holder breaches the agent ceiling was admitted, order-dependently. At this head it is refused. That is the right direction, but it is a refusal the PR body and changeset do not name. Add a FROM→TO row ("agent-account grant of a two-holder metadata-only set, only the second-listed holder over the ceiling: FROM admitted TO refused naming the breach") and list the other consumers that now see every holder on this path (`suggested-audience-bindings` proposes per holder, `cleanup-package-permissions` sees the remaining holder, `explain-engine` roster) in Acceptance notes. Text-only fix; delta review.
- nit N1: a package-less row and a `sys_metadata`-sentinel row of the same name collapse to one `''` holder, and which body is kept follows row order (first listed). The jsdoc says the order no longer follows the service's row order. Either pin which wins or narrow the sentence. Accepted as-is if you prefer; no correctness effect found (both are the environment's slot).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/core: patch` is right: no export, type or schema moves; the change is a fix of a read that already promised one entry per holder (jsdoc on `list`). `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the correct arm for the grant move; with S1 it is mixed (a widening on the grant hook and a narrowing on the agent-account ceiling), so write `Clause-②: yes (widening; narrowing on the agent-account ceiling)` or equivalent in both the PR body and the changeset. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: nothing an author can write changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author login `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); implemented by area E2 session_016WV4cyrFFk86Jqf7Mp5Rzw.
- CI at this head: `PR-body guards` red — `check:closing-target-claim`: card #32867 has no `Claim:` naming `claude/project-thread-k3e3um`. Area thread fixes on the card, not here. Test Core / Test UI still running when read (15:15Z).
- No governed path, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no ADR in the diff.

Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`

## Contract review

Head-sha: `74bc77a67ff1dc41b50928298f79a8b4cd1fad17`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts, packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/grant-permission-set-package.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/agent-account-grant-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/suggested-audience-bindings.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/cleanup-package-permissions.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/catalog-activation.ts (read only)

Delta review of `3e77d606..74bc77a6` (one commit, docs/comment only), by the reviewer of record 6879545488.

### ① Derived judgments

- S1 fixed: the PR body and changeset now carry the agent-account ceiling row (FROM admitted on the first-listed body only TO refused naming the breach, #32164 fail-closed reading every holder) and list every consumer that now sees each holder on the metadata-only path (`judgeGrantSet`, `setBreaches`, catalog-activation, the activation ledger, and the rest). Matches the code read at 3e77d606; no code moved in this delta.
- N1 resolved by stating the rule in the `list` jsdoc: a package-less row and a `sys_metadata`-provenance row are one environment holder and the first listed is kept. Accepted.
- The code diff of the PR as a whole is unchanged from the reviewed head (the only `.ts` hunk in the delta is the jsdoc).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/core: patch`; `Clause-②: yes (widening; narrowing on the agent-account ceiling)` is now the right, complete arm in both the PR body and the changeset. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author login `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); area E2 session_016WV4cyrFFk86Jqf7Mp5Rzw.
- CI at this head when read: 17 green, 17 running, 1 cancelled (superseded run). The PR-body guard (`check:closing-target-claim`, card #32867) was red at 3e77d606; the ACCEPT must re-read every check at this head.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing is the correct consequence of the fix: the agent ceiling was designed (#32164) to judge every holder of a refused name, and the metadata-only list was the one input that hid holders from it. Making the list match the registry path's shape removes an order-dependent security answer. Holds against the cited code and the card's constraint (nothing the registry path refuses is admitted).
